chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about a man who emancipated his slave girl while she was pregnant, so he said: If he knew of her pregnancy, then what is in her belly is of her status, and if he did not know, then what is in her belly is a slave.

key_terms.دَبَّرَ: Emancipated (specifically tadbir, where a slave becomes free upon the owner's death)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the child of a pregnant slave girl if her owner emancipates her?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the legal status of the offspring in the context of *tadbir* (emancipation upon death), distinguishing between the owner's knowledge of the pregnancy and the child's resulting status. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the child's status is derivative of the mother's, yet contingent on the owner's awareness, ensuring fairness in inheritance of freedom. This ruling underscores the importance of intent and knowledge in manumission cases within Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who arranged (the emancipation of) his slave girl, and she was pregnant. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he knew of her pregnancy, so whatever is in her belly would be of her status, and if he did not know, so whatever is in her belly, is a slave’.
